[IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r8] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | prefers | Ibn ʿĀshūr considers tārah an underived, frozen noun.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p240/r9] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The emergence is resurrection after the bodies have been recreated inside the earth; calling it another time points to re-creation as in the first creation, as stated at 21:104. | mentions 21:104
[TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r7] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | The pronouns refer to earth: people originate from it, return to it and become part of it, then emerge from it again to return to God, completing their guidance-cycle.
[ASAD-NOTES:20:53#n37/r1] ASAD-NOTES, d. 1412 · author | holds | Man's body is created from earth and returns to it by dissolving into its elementary organic and inorganic substances; creation, life, and dissolution show God's power, life's ephemerality, and resurrection. | mentions 3:59, 15:26
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r1] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | These four verses are God's direct insertion, not Moses's speech; the shift makes the past account address present-day Quraysh and identify their true Lord and rightful object of worship and obedience.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r2] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | The insertion informs Quraysh that the message also concerns them and asks them to recognize who deserves worship and obedience.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r5] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | God's providence entails a Judgment Day where those who meet their obligations are rewarded and those who spread disorder misuse His favors are punished.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r6] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | Resurrection is no difficulty for the one who first created humanity from earth.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p44/r1] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | The first-person wording confirms that the inserted verses are God's words, not part of Moses's conversation.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r14] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | The verse recalls that humans came from earth, return to it, and will be brought back to life from it after death.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r15] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | rejects | The verse does not support reincarnation, despite attempts to use it and similar verses for that claim; see 2:28. | mentions 2:28
[STUDYQURAN:20:55/r1] STUDYQURAN · author | holds | The pronoun refers either to the earth or to dust, which can also mean earth. | mentions 43:11
[STUDYQURAN:20:55/r2] STUDYQURAN · author | holds | The verse is often recited at Muslim funerals to recall that people are made from earth or clay, buried in it, and resurrected from it.

<<end of notes>>
